newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 22.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Royal Thai Air Force (RTAF) is seeking a direct equity holding in the state-owned New Bangkok International Airport Co Ltd (NBIA) as the Nong Ngu Hao airport project appears headed towards a revamp. Sources say that the success of the RTAF's equity plan will be linked to any agreement to move the Air Force base from its present location adjacent to Don Muang International Airport as part of a plan to expand that site for commercial use, a move which received Cabinet approval yesterday. (THE NATION, BUSINESS DAY)

- The constitution drafting committee will listen to opinions from Members of Parliament to widen its outlook, and MPs must at the same time accept public opinions to be used as a basis for the new constitution though they may stand to lose some interests, committee chairman Anand Panyarachun says. (BANGKOK POST)

- Education Minister Sukhavich Rangsitphol remains a staunch supporter of the Rajabhat Institute's ban on homosexual students, despite protests by homosexual and human rights organisations. Some 200 rights groups have decried the teachers training college's move to bar homosexuals from their 36 campuses nationwide. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- Thai Satellite Telecommunications, an affiliate of United Communication Group, says its global mobile phone satellite system is expected to be operational in September 1998 as planned. This is despite several launching postponements of the first of 73 satellites. The launch was delayed again due to the explosion of a Delta Two rocket carrying a U.S. military satellite at an Air Force base in Florida last weekend. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The cabinet has endorsed a proposal by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan appointing Ekamol Khiriwat to the board of directors of the Bank of Thailand, effective January 1. Ekamol was formerly deputy governor of the Bank of Thailand and head of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). He was removed from the SEC on accusation of leaking confidential financial information. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)
